text:
jordan: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on capacity: a few customers asked about region priority and how we avoid flip-flopping when multiple regions report low idle. Can we summarize the behavior here?

tara: TL;DR: we have a hysteresis window + cooldown to avoid thrash. Order is local -> region-group -> global, but we only move to the next hop if the upstream metric breach persists for the stabilization window.

jordan: Stabilization window = ?

tara: Defaults: evaluation_window=90s, hysteresis_margin=15% (so usage must exceed threshold by 15% for it to be considered). Cooldown after a move = 3m. These are adjustable per-customer in the policy.

sam: How do region-groups map? For example, APAC fallback list?

tara: APAC group = [ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-south-1]. Next hop after APAC is global (primarily EU/US pools). Mapping is in the region_map config in infra repo.

priya: Curious about preemption: if a spot GPU gets reclaimed in EU while serving APAC-burst, do we fail-over or reshard?

tara: We prefer transparent failover. The runtime keeps a coroutine-level retry path: if preemption occurs we try the next weighted region. We avoid resharding long-lived KV cache across regions because that costs too much latency.

cory: Any procurement timeline updates? We heard from HW that next rack shipments for APAC slipped. Impact?

sam: HW update from earlier: APAC rack ETA moved from late May -> mid-June due to board shortages. We added a 10% safety buffer to existing schedules but this might shift Dedicated ramp plans by a week or two.

jordan: Does that change default burst policy for APAC? I.e., will we more aggressively spill to same-continent vs. global?

tara: Yes — we increased same-continent weight by +0.2 for APAC through the procurement window. It's a temporary tweak and we'll rollback when on-prem inventory arrives.

priya: Can we expose a simple summary to customers: "expected fallback chain for your region"? That would help support.

sam: We can auto-generate a short table per-customer based on their pinned region and allow_spill flag. Docs team is already on it.

jordan: Ops question: if multiple customers spill to the same donor region, do we throttle based on per-customer tier?

tara: Yes. Donor region admission controller enforces per-customer rate and a global fairness slider. Tiers get priority but we enforce absolute caps to protect latency SLOs for resident traffic.

infra-bot: Note: observed donor pressure event at 2026-03-10T02:11Z where EU donor queue increased 45%. No customer-facing errors; automated throttles engaged. See INC-2026-271.

cory: Thanks. Last one from me: for enterprise customers on Private, will we backport the same hysteresis/cooldown logic to the private agent?

tara: We're shipping a v0.9 agent update with the same logic as an opt-in feature (agent.policy.allow_remote_donor = false by default). Private customers can opt into cross-site spill with the update.

jordan: Great. Can someone drop the policy snippet + a short FAQ in the all-hands doc? I'll forward to the customer success threads.

priya: I'll prepare a 2-paragraph FAQ and a diagram. Sam, can you share the procurement note with CS?

sam: On it. I'll post the hardware ETA and affected SKUs in #customer-success in 30m.

jordan: Perfect. If anything changes overnight ping me and add to the all-hands followups. Thanks all.
